data.narrative:
Cellares is a Series C biotech company that has raised $350M+. The valuation analysis draws on a peer set of 3 same-sector, same-stage private comparables (Colossal Biosciences at $10.3B, Chai Discovery at $3.8B, and New Limit at $3.1B), plus 3 public Biotech & Health companies (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) for directional context.

Two quantitative methods triangulate to a range. The Stage-Progression method, applying a 1.7x step-up multiplier to the $12M total-raised proxy, implies $20M. The Peer-Median method anchors to the $3.8B median valuation across the three same-stage private comparables, with a peer range of $3.1B to $10.3B. Public-comp anchoring via P/S multiples (median 9.2x in the sector) cannot be applied without disclosed revenue figures, which private companies typically do not publish. These two applicable methods produce a triangulated range of $17M (low) to $4.4B (high), with a median of $1.9B.

The wide spread reflects structural uncertainty: early-stage biotech valuations cluster around peer outcomes and stage progression, but Cellares' position within its peer cohort remains unclear without granular data on clinical progress, IP position, or capital efficiency. The peer-median method carries greater weight given the comparable stage and sector alignment. Key uncertainties include technology de-risking trajectory and relative competitive positioning within the Colossal–Chai–New Limit range.
